accepted.expected_invariant: API remains available and responds to health checks within a short recovery window after a pod kill.
accepted.hypothesis: The API service is a single instance with no replicas and depends on multiple critical backends. A pod kill will cause a full API outage until the container restarts, and because there is no healthcheck on the API (only a restart policy), the orchestrator may not detect the failure promptly, leading to a longer downtime than necessary.
accepted.recovery_expectation: Container restarts due to restart:always; API should recover automatically, but downtime may be longer due to lack of healthcheck.
accepted.validation_plan: Baseline: verify API health endpoint returns 200. Inject pod_kill on api. Observe API availability and container restart. Oracle: check that API recovers within expected restart policy time and health endpoint returns 200.
accepted.weakness_surface: Single point of failure at the API service; lack of healthcheck delays failure detection and recovery.
accepted.workload_contract: API readiness plus mock workflow response

accepted.expected_invariant: API and worker continue to function or fail gracefully when agent_backend is unavailable.
accepted.hypothesis: agent_backend is a critical dependency for api and worker, but it has no healthcheck and only a restart policy. A pod kill will cause all dependent services to lose functionality until restart completes, and without healthcheck, the system may not detect the failure quickly, leading to cascading timeouts.
accepted.recovery_expectation: agent_backend restarts due to restart:always; dependent services may recover after restart, but may experience errors during downtime.
accepted.validation_plan: Baseline: verify API and worker health. Inject pod_kill on agent_backend. Observe API and worker behavior. Oracle: check if API returns errors or timeouts; check if worker tasks fail.
accepted.weakness_surface: agent_backend is a single point of failure with no healthcheck; dependent services (api, worker) may not handle its unavailability gracefully.
accepted.workload_contract: API readiness plus mock workflow response

accepted.expected_invariant: API and worker continue to operate normally or fail gracefully when Redis is unavailable.
accepted.hypothesis: Redis is a shared dependency for api, agent_backend, worker, and worker_beat. A pod kill will cause cache misses, session loss, and potential queue disruption. Since Redis has a healthcheck and restart policy, recovery may be quick, but the impact on dependent services could be significant if they do not handle Redis unavailability gracefully.
accepted.recovery_expectation: Redis restarts due to restart:always; dependent services may recover after restart, but may experience errors during downtime.
accepted.validation_plan: Baseline: verify API and worker functionality. Inject pod_kill on redis. Observe API and worker behavior. Oracle: check if API returns errors or timeouts; check if worker tasks fail.
accepted.weakness_surface: Redis is a critical shared dependency; its failure can cause cascading failures across multiple services.
accepted.workload_contract: API readiness plus mock workflow response

accepted.recovery_expectation: MySQL restarts due to restart:always; dependent services may recover after restart, but may experience errors during downtime.
accepted.validation_plan: Baseline: verify API and worker functionality. Inject pod_kill on db_mysql. Observe API and worker behavior. Oracle: check if API returns errors or timeouts; check if worker tasks fail.

accepted.workload_contract: API readiness plus mock workflow response

accepted.expected_invariant: API responses remain within acceptable latency bounds under network delay.
accepted.hypothesis: The API service has no healthcheck and depends on multiple backends. Introducing network delay on the API's outbound connections may cause timeouts and degraded performance, but without healthcheck, the system may not detect the degradation and continue to route traffic to a slow API.
accepted.recovery_expectation: After removing delay, API should return to normal latency; no persistent impact expected.
accepted.validation_plan: Baseline: measure API response time. Inject network_delay on api. Observe API response time and health. Oracle: check if response time exceeds acceptable threshold or if health endpoint fails.
accepted.weakness_surface: Lack of healthcheck on API; network delay can cause timeouts and degraded performance without detection.
accepted.workload_contract: API readiness plus mock workflow response
